office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Second-term Democrat Joe Timmons, who voted against the 2026 income tax but sees merit in a millionaires' tax, faces first-time Republican candidate Justin Pike, a sheriff's detective running on budget accountability and lower taxes. Timmons won 54% in the primary, and the two have raised similar amounts.

candidates.summary: Second-term State Representative, Assistant Speaker Pro Tempore and former aide to Gov. Inslee, focused on state investment in Whatcom County, higher-education funding and housing supply.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 (2026 income tax) and the 2025 B&O and services tax bills, citing too little relief from other taxes [S7][S9][S10][S14]
Prime sponsor of HB 2070 for Western Washington University funding parity [S11]
States he is "100% Pro-Choice" and supports continued emissions reductions [S3]
Voted for ESHB 1296, the parental-rights rewrite I-1 would undo [S8]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346, EHB 2081 and ESSB 5814; says he sees merit in a millionaires' tax but wants drastic cuts to sales, B&O and property taxes alongside any new revenue.

spending.basis: Campaigns on securing state funding for local projects and sponsors WWU funding parity; also cited state spending levels in his income-tax vote.

housing.basis: Website centers building more housing near transit, while he voted for the EHB 1217 rent-increase limits.

climate.basis: Says climate change is real and supports continued emissions reductions and the clean-energy economy; endorsed by Sierra Club and Washington Conservation Action; no stated position on carbon pricing.

healthcare.basis: Cites work to lower EpiPen and inhaler costs and a medical-debt bill, measures within the existing insurance system.

immigration.basis: Voted yes on SB 5855 limiting face coverings worn by law enforcement; no campaign statement on immigration.

social.basis: States he is 100% pro-choice and that abortion decisions belong to patients and providers; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Advocates.

parental-rights.basis: Voted yes on ESHB 1296, which amended the I-2081 parental-rights law, on House passage and final passage; no statement on notification or opt-outs.

experience.basis: Second House term, Assistant Speaker Pro Tempore and 15 years in government, facing a first-time candidate.

candidates.summary: Whatcom County Sheriff's detective, National Guard soldier and Ferndale small-business owner running for office for the first time on affordability, budget accountability and public safety.
highlights: Opposes tax increases and calls for rebalancing the state tax structure [S3][S7]
Would speed permitting, reassess energy-efficiency mandates and let Growth Management Act boundaries expand with growth [S3]
Supports enforcement and repeat-offender accountability alongside behavioral-health treatment [S2][S3]
Criticizes the Climate Commitment Act's cost and reporting [S8]

taxes.basis: Platform says excessive taxation holds back business; opposed raising taxes at a May town hall and says the Climate Commitment Act taxed people out of their homes.

spending.basis: Starts accountability with the budget, criticizes one-time funding of ongoing programs and overspending, and calls for measurable results.

housing.basis: Housing platform is faster permitting, fewer energy-efficiency mandates and easier boundary expansion under the Growth Management Act.

local-control.basis: Wants the Growth Management Act changed so municipal boundaries expand with local growth rather than on state multi-decade schedules.

safety.basis: Supports effective law enforcement and accountability for repeat offenders, combined with shelter, treatment and community service for minor offenses.

climate.basis: Criticizes the Climate Commitment Act's cost and would reassess energy-efficiency mandates on homeowners.

experience.basis: First-time candidate for public office facing a second-term incumbent.
